title: Boundary-Sensitive Quantum Order on Non-Amenable Lattices
authors: Xingzhi Wang, Zohar Nussinov, Gerardo Ortiz
abstract: We show that quantum systems on non-amenable lattices, whose boundaries constitute an extensive fraction of the system, host novel forms of bulk ordering with no Euclidean counterpart. Combining boundary-retaining iDMRG with an exact symmetry-fixing duality, we investigate $p<5$ state clock models on the coordination-3 infinite Cayley tree. We find that between the ordered and disordered phases lies an emergent intermediate phase with bulk order induced by an arbitrarily weak boundary field rather than by conventional spontaneous symmetry-breaking. This establishes boundary-sensitive order as a distinct quantum ordering mechanism defying Landau's spontaneous symmetry-breaking paradigm. The intermediate phase realizes a bulk-boundary correspondence in which the unpolarized boundary selects a specific ordered bulk state.
summary: This work explores quantum ordering on complex, non-amenable lattices using the $p$-state clock model. The authors demonstrate a novel 'boundary-sensitive' order in an intermediate phase, where the bulk state is dictated by the boundary condition even when the system appears symmetric. This challenges the traditional understanding of phase transitions based solely on spontaneous symmetry breaking.
main_problem: The paper investigates novel forms of bulk quantum ordering in systems defined on non-amenable lattices that cannot be explained by conventional Landau spontaneous symmetry-breaking theory.
main_result: They establish the existence of a boundary-sensitive quantum order in an intermediate phase, where bulk order is induced by an arbitrarily weak boundary field rather than by symmetry breaking.
method: The study combines boundary-retaining iDMRG techniques with an exact symmetry-fixing duality to analyze the quantum $p$-state clock model.
model_or_system: The system is the quantum $p$-state clock model ($p \ge 2$) Hamiltonian studied on the coordination-3 infinite Cayley tree, a non-amenable lattice.
key_observables: Boundary-bond entanglement entropy ($S_\partial$), central polarization ($m_0$), and the comparison of bulk observables in boundary-biased versus symmetric states.
important_parameters: The ratio of coupling strengths $K = J/h$ and the boundary bias $B_\partial = h_\partial/h$, analyzed in the limit $B_\partial 	o 0^+$.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires treating the full boundary-retained quantum system, as standard bulk optimization methods fail to capture the extensive boundary effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum phase diagram for $p=2$ and $p=3$, showing the intermediate phase, and demonstrate boundary-to-bulk propagation of magnetization profiles.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using symmetry-fixing duality and bond-algebraic mapping. It then applies infinite-DMRG schemes to the Cayley tree and its dual to calculate observables, culminating in the characterization of the three distinct quantum phases.
why_interesting: The concept of boundary-sensitive order provides a new mechanism for quantum phase transitions, suggesting that boundary conditions can dictate bulk physics in ways that defy standard mean-field or symmetry-breaking paradigms.
